description: Closed OHLCV bars as persisted, one row per (provider, symbol, side, timeframe, bar_start_ts). A window occupies two rows, one per price side, written in a single transaction. Written only by its owning service, which also owns this table's DDL and migrations; read by historical-query-svc as a declared read-side consumer. Evolution within this version lineage is additive only.

hypertable.rationale: About 2.3M rows per day across all timeframes and both sides, so a week per chunk stays comfortable while keeping chunk exclusion useful for the range queries historical-query serves.

columns.name: side
columns.description: 'bid' or 'ask'. A typed column rather than a key inside a JSONB price document, so the schema stays visible to information_schema, to the shared fixture, and to the destructive-migration check.

columns.name: bar_start_ts
columns.description: The hypertable's time dimension, and part of the upsert key. Aligned to the timeframe boundary.

columns.name: tick_count
columns.description: Identical on a window's two side-rows; 0 marks an idle bar carried forward.

columns.name: is_closed
columns.description: Always true in this table, since only closed bars are persisted. Kept as a column because the contract record carries it and historical-query filters on it explicitly; not constrained, because dropping a CHECK later would be a destructive change.

indexes.name: bars_provider_symbol_side_timeframe_bar_start_ts_idx
indexes.description: The documented access path and the idempotent-upsert key. Unique is legal here, unlike on ticks, because the tuple already contains the partitioning column.

notes: The upsert key and the index are the same tuple: bar-persistence upserts on conflict against it, so the unique index is what makes a redelivered closed bar overwrite in place rather than duplicate.
